rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, Table 2 - the authors acquired an EO-1 Hyperion image over Mackay (2 April 2002), computed 40 narrow-band indices on 142 diseased and 159 non-diseased sample pixels and ran discriminant function analysis with a 30% hold-out sample; this is the study's own data and analysis.
rows.notes: The study only shows that Hyperion-derived indices (notably the newly formulated DWSI-1, DWSI-2, DWSI-5 and MSI) can discriminate sugarcane blocks severely affected (severity 4 of 5) by orange rust from non-diseased blocks of the same variety and age, with hold-out classification accuracies up to ~95% per index and 96.9% for the combined discriminant function. It reports detection/mapping of an existing disease only; it does not report any farmer action, control measure, or prevention of further damage resulting from the detection (the link to chemical control is only asserted in the introduction). The claim's function is pest_control, so the study supports only the precondition (detection) of the claimed effect. The authors themselves note that early-stage (low to moderate severity) detection was not tested and that water-stressed but uninfected crops could confound the indices, but these limitations concern detection, not control.

notes: Full text appears complete (short Letter, 10 pages). Single image date, single region, single crop and cultivar; no field measurements of biophysical variables, ground reference limited to field officers' severity ratings.
